narratives.Overview:
1. No `.deft/approved-scope` record is written for scope. `isHumanApprovalStamp` is not on this path. `authz:grant` keeps the phrase mint. Proceed writes nothing and needs no token set. `scope:record-approved-scope` is not invoked for proceed or for a later expansion.
2. The fence is the active brief's `file_scope` on the merge base. The declaration on that base is agent-authored. The fence is a drift check against that precommitment, not a human authorization of the list. Two builds carry it. A merge-time check compares changed files with the base brief and does not read the head brief. A write fence reads that same base brief and fails closed when the brief cannot be read. A pull request that adds production paths and edits its own active brief to include them fails `task check`. The planner's declaration is on the base before the worker branches. The worker is a later process and cannot widen that base list.
3. Paths under a configured test root pass and spend nothing. The fence and the budget apply to production roots only.
4. The production allowance is a count of concrete production files on the merge base, floor 2, cap 5. A glob entry is not a concrete file. Paths inside the cap land. Paths past the cap split to a follow-up story. That remainder is an independently valid change, or that story stays blocked and is replanned. No prompt. Unrelated and low-confidence are not selectors. Parent text and model output are not an allow input. `scopeExpansion` does not return `remediationForRenewedApproval`.
5. There is no pre-Wave-1 root-count refusal. A protected-glob hit is #4980. This remedy does not define the class checks.
6. `scope-provenance.md`, `deft-directive-swarm`, and the AGENTS managed text say that after proceed there is no scope ceremony to schedule.

issueCommentThread.body:
## Analysis

The mint stops in this session are the scope gate doing what it was told, on a workflow the gate was not shaped for. They are not a maintainer exemption, and they are not a regression that landed in 0.119.6.

`verify:scope-provenance` hard-fails only when an **active** brief is **in the change set**, has a **non-empty** `file_scope`, and has no human digest already on the merge base. A brief with no `file_scope` warns, and `task check` still exits 0. There is no role check in that predicate.

### Why a maintainer "take through merge issue N" never mints

The product pull request is the code. The brief usually has no `file_scope` while that pull request is open, or it is not in the pull request at all.

- #4824's product pull request #4829 contains no xBRIEF and no `.deft/approved-scope` file. The brief arrived later, already under `xbrief/completed/`, which this gate does not read. That completed brief does list paths. There is still no digest for its plan id.
- #4950's product pull request #4954 committed an active brief whose metadata is the issue thread. There is no `swarm.file_scope`.

Nothing declared means nothing to freeze. `content/docs/scope-provenance.md` says the same thing from the other side: if the operator is not going to mint, omit `file_scope` when the brief is written. An empty story scope also installs no story write fence, so this path has no visibility when a list shows up later.

### Why #4956 minted

This session did not hand the agent an existing issue. On NoteTechnic, pin 0.119.6, the instruction was to swarm M1-13..M1-17 through merge. The agent created the issues and wrote swarm-ready briefs. A swarm-ready story must have a non-empty `file_scope`. Those active briefs were in the tree before Wave 1. That is the input the gate hard-fails.

The deposited contract then requires a human digest on the merge base before implement, says an in-harness "please proceed" is not that digest, and forbids deleting the list to get back to the warning (#3874). Four stories, no batch verb, so four `scope:record-approved-scope` stops. After those digests were on `main` (chore #332), Greptile grew the path lists and #4589 demanded `--kind renewed-approval` (chore #337). M1-17 asked again after Wave 1. The phrase `mint` is the #3110 human-presence gate, reused by #3384. Nothing in the 0.119.3–0.119.6 changelog adds this first-mint stop. #4589 was already in 0.119.1.

Adjacent, not the same issue: #3718 (readiness wants `file_scope`, provenance then wants a prior merged mint; `swarm:launch` stays unreachable), #4383 (first-mint activate digest, still open), #4589 (expansion remint, shipped and working as specified).

### Original pains the ceremony was built for

**#3145** (consumer, Directive v0.93). The implementation pull request added a `test_*.py` script under `infra/scripts/`, pointed a deployment script at `tests/fixtures/`, added smoke-test cloud identities to infrastructure templates, and placed a smoke-evidence class under `Tools`. The same pull request edited the active xBRIEF so those paths were in scope. `verify:forward-coverage` then passed, because it only asks whether each changed file is mentioned by the brief. Gates stayed green. Test harnesses and cloud permissions shipped inside production delivery.

The scope acceptance line is: a pull request cannot authorize new paths by editing its own active xBRIEF. Any new path needed renewed human approval. The issue also says reviewer attention is not the enforcement mechanism. The additions were a handful of paths. A count allowance by itself would have passed that pull request.

**#3110.** Under an active UAT lease, an agent shell could run `authz:grant` with no TTY and unlock Write / push / PR / merge. The typed phrase on a real terminal exists so the agent shell cannot complete that command.

**#3384.** `scope:record-approved-scope` must use that same gate, and `--actor` is display only, so an agent cannot satisfy #3145 by stamping its own digest. `isHumanApprovalStamp` is a string check on `kind` and `actor`. An agent that can Write JSON can emit `kind: operator` and a matching digest. The merge-base rule is what stops same-PR self-authorization. The phrase does not prove the file on the base was produced by the CLI. Under a human merge gate, the second look is a person merging the approval commit. A chore pull request merged unread is the same event as a forged JSON.

### What the current ceremony actually does

Both recorded sessions miss the only thing the digest is for: a path list a person looked at before that list became the fence.

- Maintainer issue flow: the list is absent while the code merges, then it can appear on the completed brief with no prompt.
- #4956: the human is stopped mid-cohort and types `mint` to get the swarm moving, without reading the paths. A skip or approve at that moment is the same rubber stamp.

The pull request diff is the surface people already review. A terminal phrase in the middle of Greptile babysit is not.

## Suggested way forward

Keep the human out of the running loop. Fail in the machine. Do not offer skip or approve when a story overflows. The typed `mint` stays on `authz:grant` (#3110) and comes off scope.

**1. Class check, outside any budget.** On every diff, including the first pull request, fail closed for a test artifact under a production root, a production reference to a test root, or a test-only identity or role binding. That is the #3145 damage, and it was small. `verify:test-boundary` still warns until a project policy sets `enforce`, so these classes have to fail the pull request or that incident still merges green. A glob, or a protected path (hooks, authz, the verifier, publish policy), fails the same way. Nobody is asked to approve it.

**2. Freeze the declared list at proceed.** Dispatch writes the record from the `file_scope` already on the briefs. Workers do not. If that list already fails the class check, refuse dispatch once, before Wave 1, and name the paths. An ordinary list does not prompt. After that, a changed file outside the frozen list fails check. Editing `file_scope` in the same pull request does not make the check pass. One automatic exception: a test file in a test root that belongs to a source file already frozen, and `CHANGELOG.md`.

**3. One small Greptile allowance, from that frozen list, until the pull request merges.** The budget is the larger of 2 files and 20% of the frozen concrete list, and it never exceeds 5.

| Frozen list | 20% | Budget |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 3–10 paths | 1–2 | 2 |
| 15 paths | 3 | 3 |
| 20 paths | 4 | 4 |
| 25 or more | 5+ | 5 |

Two is the floor so a three-file story can still take a missed caller and one neighbor. Five is the cap so a large list cannot quietly grow by a tenth of a subsystem. The count does not reset on each Greptile push. Paired tests and `CHANGELOG.md` do not spend it. Class violations do not spend it either. They fail. A bare five, or a percentage alone, is the wrong budget: #3145 fits inside five files, and a percentage of a large list is a large silent expansion.

**4. Over budget, the leaf does not ask the end user.** It sends the frozen list, the extra paths, and the diff to the orchestrator. The parent classifies each extra path. TypeSafe (Jev Choice) fits that closed set when credentials exist: caller of a frozen file, paired test, unrelated subsystem, or class violation. Code applies the answers. A class violation is refused before the model is asked, and a model "yes" does not put it back. Callers spend the budget. Past the budget they still leave this pull request, and the account says they are real callers and they are the follow-up. Unrelated paths always split. Low confidence splits too. It does not become "approve or skip."

A critic may write the paragraph the user reads. It cannot waive the check. If it can, an agent has approved an agent, which is the hole #3110 and #3145 closed.

The user hears it once, when the pull request is ready: which paths Greptile added, which stayed, which were held out, why, and the follow-up that owns the rest. Doing nothing keeps the fence. Taking the held-out paths is starting that follow-up, which freezes a new list at a story boundary.

**5. No frozen list.** The usual maintainer first pull request. Class check only. No mint. After merge, the closer may record the paths that shipped so a later pull request on that same brief has a baseline. That record does not authorize the pull request already merged. The budget arms only on the later pull request.

### What this would have done to the recorded pains

- **#3145.** The script under `infra/scripts/` and the fixture reference fail the class check. The brief edit fails the scope check, because those paths were not in the list frozen before the pull request, and the edit cannot legalize them. The agent is not offered a phrase.
- **#4956.** "Swarm M1-13..17, proceed" freezes each declared list and starts the workers. No per-story mint, no chore pull requests #332 and #337. A couple of writer call sites stay inside the two-file floor. A wider ripple splits, per story. M1-17 does not ask for a first approval after Wave 1. The other stories are not blocked.
- **Maintainer through-merge.** Unchanged on the first pull request. A later widening of a recorded list uses the same budget and the same split. No terminal session in the middle of the run.

Reviewed proposal comment 5798533764 against Stop 1 comment 5800234289 and panel deposit 5800252810. HEAD equals cae371d0161bb7c03df0ab9fc312c477f7c524cc. Repository evidence below was read with git show at that SHA. No later comments or sibling critiques were consulted.

## Dispatch is a role, not an independent approval boundary
blocks-the-design
Evidence: In packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts, baseApprovalAuthorizesCurrent reads the base record and checks its binding and agreement with the current record. content/docs/scope-provenance.md explicitly rejects same-change-set approval creation or rewriting. I executed the SHA-pinned digest.ts using Node's type stripping: isHumanApprovalStamp({kind:'operator', actor:'invented-human'}) returns true; kind:'dispatch' returns false. The proposal itself correctly acknowledges that stamp strings are forgeable. Its replacement says dispatch writes the frozen record, workers do not, and removes the prior approval chore PRs, but supplies no independently enforced writer or immutable reference.
Failure mode: A worker able to write the replacement record can enlarge the list or replace its identity before check, using only ordinary source paths that pass the class check. Calling that write dispatch, or asking a parent agent to do it, does not make it independent. Keeping the existing base-record requirement instead would still reject a fresh dispatch-only record, restoring the startup dependency the remedy removes. A hash authenticates neither the author nor the proceed event.
Disposition: Before bind, identify the trusted proceed capture and the authority read by CI, including how a worker cannot replace or replay the cohort/story binding or reset its baseline. This can reuse an independently controlled base or host surface; it need not prescribe a new signing system. Retaining a typed phrase is not my requirement. A demonstrated worker-write/redispatch refusal with a valid in-harness proceed succeeding would resolve this finding.

## Enforcing test-boundary is not the full proposed class check
sharpens-framing
Evidence: I materialized SHA-pinned modules and their local imports into an OS-temp directory, stripped TypeScript types with Node 24, and called evaluateTestBoundary with defaultTestBoundaryPolicy('enforce'). A test at infra/scripts/test_smoke.py returned exit 1, test-under-source-root. An infra/deploy.sh reference to tests/fixtures/probe.py returned exit 1, production-references-test-root. An infra/main.bicep declaring a user-assigned identity named smoke-test-identity returned exit 0 with no findings. The evaluator's violation-kind union contains only placement and reference checks; policy.ts also supplies allow entries and test-root exceptions.
Failure mode: Implementing the proposal as merely switching the existing verifier from warn to enforce leaves the identity example green, including on the explicitly unfrozen first-PR path. A claim that this alone covers the named #3145 classes would overstate the protection.
Disposition: The design can retain a new class check, but its scope must explicitly include an additional identity/role-binding detector and the trusted source of classification policy. Keep ordinary language-specific test-root exceptions distinct from production pollution. My probe establishes a missing existing capability, not that the proposed detector is impossible or that a full historical #3145 replay was performed.

## A required caller cannot always be split into a later deliverable
sharpens-framing
Evidence: Proposal sections 3-4 cap the allowance at five and require even real callers beyond budget to leave the PR. A concrete counterexample follows directly: a frozen source changes a public signature and six previously unlisted callers must change atomically; paired tests are exempt, but the sixth caller is not. The existing scope and test-boundary mechanisms inventory supplies no transformation that makes that partial change valid.
Failure mode: Removing the sixth caller can leave a broken build or behavior. Keeping quality gates correctly blocks that PR; filing a follow-up does not make the first PR mergeable. Thus automatic split does not imply uninterrupted completion of each original story.
Disposition: Retain the cap, but state that split means a independently valid remainder, such as a compatible staged change. Otherwise the affected story stays blocked or is rolled back and replanned, with its dependent stories held. This sharpens the completion promise without requiring another approval prompt or a budget waiver.

It returns true for kind `operator`, `human`, `user`, `cli`, `github-user`, `interactive`, `renewed-approval`, or any kind prefixed `human`, unless the actor is `agent`, `agent:…`, or `self`. `evaluateScopeProvenance` hard-fails a non-empty `file_scope` when the active brief is in the change set and the merge-base `.deft/approved-scope/<plan-id>.json` is missing, non-human, digest-mismatched, or rewritten in that same change set (`active-xbrief-modified-without-digest`, `self-authorizing-scope-expansion`). Empty `file_scope` is the warn path and exits 0. `APPROVED_SCOPE_DIR` is `.deft/approved-scope` inside the repo, and `writeApprovedScopeRecord` only writes that JSON. `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` and `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES` in `packages/core/src/check/gate-lists.ts` both run `verify:scope-provenance`. `content/docs/scope-provenance.md` says an allocation-context token is not provenance and the digest is on the merge base before workers activate. Comment 5798533764 step 2 says dispatch writes the record from the briefs, workers do not, and chore pull requests #332 and #337 go away.
Failure mode: Proceed copies the agent-written `file_scope` into a record. Committed on the implement pull request, the same-change-set rule fails check. Committed earlier, that commit is the chore pull request this design removes, and kind `dispatch` still fails the stamp, so the session stops on `scope:record-approved-scope`. Held only in parent memory, CI and the other story worktrees never read it, and check still exits 1. Writing kind `operator` from dispatch is the self-stamp the target says it withholds. A glob the agent put on the brief becomes the authority. Proceed does not carry the path list.
Disposition: The authority record stays the merge-base `.deft/approved-scope/<plan-id>.json` that `baseApprovalAuthorizesCurrent` already reads. A dispatch write must keep failing `isHumanApprovalStamp`, and a same-PR rewrite must keep hard-failing. A proceed copy of the brief is not that record. Until the design names a record that meets those two existing predicates, the no-mint claim cannot bind.

## The class check does not fail the #3145 set
blocks-the-design
Evidence: `TestBoundaryViolationKind` in `packages/core/src/test-boundary/evaluate.ts` is only `test-under-source-root` and `production-references-test-root`. `evaluateTestBoundary` lists the tracked tree with `git ls-files`, skips any `policy.allow` hit, and exits 0 when `enforcementMode` is `warn`. `defaultTestBoundaryPolicy` is warn. `loadTestBoundaryPolicy` reads `.deft/test-boundary.policy.json` or `plan.policy.testBoundary` from the working tree. A search of the test-boundary sources and docs at this SHA found no detector for a test-only identity or role binding. `pathishIsProtectedDest` in `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts` is a shell-destination scan for `.deft/authz`, `.deft/approved-scope`, and kill-switch names. It is not a diff check for hooks, the verifier, or publish policy. Comment 5798533764 says those classes fail outside any budget, and that `verify:test-boundary` still warns until a project sets enforce.
Failure mode: Bound to the existing checker, a `test_*.py` under `infra/scripts/` and a deploy script that mentions `tests/fixtures/` are warnings, exit 0, and the pull request still merges. A same-PR allow entry, or `enforcementMode: warn` in the policy file, clears them because the checker reads the policy in the diff. Smoke-test cloud identities, and a Tools class whose basename is not a test pattern, produce no finding. Flipping the default from warn to enforce scans the whole tracked tree, so already-present violations fail unrelated pull requests. The identity half of the #3145 incident still merges.
Disposition: Before bind, the class check names a diff-scoped detector for each of those four artifacts, and it reads allow and enforce from the merge base the same way approved-scope already does. A same-PR policy edit must fail. Switching the whole-tree default from warn to enforce is not that detector.

## The capped allowance is an agent allow
blocks-the-design
Evidence: `runtimeAuthorityForDirectWrite` in `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` loads the live brief through `loadStoryWriteFenceFromPath` and denies a classifiable direct write that misses `storyAllowPaths` (`deny-story-scope` from `evaluateRuntimeAuthorityPath`). A null path is allowed by `evaluateRuntimeAuthorityDirectWrite`. Story-fence load failure fails open to an empty scope, and an inactive fence allows the write. `storyAllowPaths` match as globs. `expectedTestPaths` in `packages/core/src/forward-coverage/correspondence.ts` is the existing source-to-test pairing. No function under `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/` classifies a caller. Comment 5798533764 says the parent classifies each extra path, TypeSafe when credentials exist, and code applies the answers. Callers spend the larger of 2 and 20% of the frozen concrete list, capped at 5. Paired tests and `CHANGELOG.md` do not spend it. The count does not reset, and sibling stories are separate.
Failure mode: The parent is an agent, and the leaf diff is untrusted input. The caller label admits up to five files with no human stamp. Refusing a class violation before the model leaves every other path on that label. With no credentials the same parent still classifies. On a hook host, a file outside the live brief is denied, and editing the brief so the write succeeds is the expansion `verify:scope-provenance` already rejects, so the allowance is either unwritable or a brief edit check fails. One glob counts as one budget path and matches every file under it, so those files never spend the cap. Twenty percent of a list that is not a multiple of five is not an integer file count. ## Background

During a NoteTechnic Grok Build swarm session on **2026-09-22/23** (Directive **0.119.6**), the operator gave an explicit proceed instruction to swarm the remaining M1-13..M1-17 cohort through merge. The Directive maintainer later agreed that this session’s behavior was **not the intended consumer experience**: that initial “please proceed / swarm this cohort” guidance should have been something the agent took and ran with (as remembered under ≤0.119.2), without forcing the operator to leave the harness repeatedly for terminal `deft scope:record-approved-scope` ceremonies.

This is a **swarm-path / proceed-consent** defect. It is related to, but not the same as, setup mid-build mint pain (#4383), renewal remint leftovers (#4589 / #4599), or `swarm:launch` readiness/`file_scope` collision (#3718). Those issues are cited as adjacent; this report is the atomic “operator proceed → uninterrupted swarm” failure.

## Environment

- **Consumer:** `deftai/notetechnic` (pnpm monorepo)
- **Directive pin / engine:** `@deftai/directive` / `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.6`
- **Host:** Grok Build (interactive harness); parent-retained swarm, leaves `stop-at: pr-open`
- **Work:** cohort `m1-13-17` — issues #327–#331, product PRs #333–#336 + #338, digest PRs #332 / #337
- **Operator action that should have been enough:** explicit proceed to swarm M1-13..M1-17 to completion (plus a subsequent in-harness cohort option selection: “Full M1-13..17 cohort”)
- **Forced out-of-harness actions observed:**
  1. **Four first-adoption scope approvals** after xBRIEFs were written/activated and *before* Wave1 dispatch:
     `deft scope:record-approved-scope -- <active xbrief> --actor polfer --confirm` (typed phrase `mint`) for m1-13, m1-14, m1-15, m1-16
  2. **Two mid-flight renewed approvals** after Greptile residuals expanded `file_scope` (mounts/writer call sites):
     `deft scope:record-approved-scope --kind renewed-approval -- …` for m1-13 and m1-15
  3. **Additional ask** for m1-17 first approval after Wave1 landed (operator declined the prompt; docs PR still merged)
- Digests landed via chore PRs (#332 first mint; #337 renewed) so implement PRs could satisfy `verify:scope-provenance` locally

## Description

### What the operator experienced

1. Operator: “swarm M1-13..17 / please proceed.”
2. Agent formed issues + swarm-ready xBRIEFs with declared `swarm.file_scope`.
3. Agent **stopped**, asked the operator to **leave the Grok harness**, open a real TTY, and run **N separate** `scope:record-approved-scope` commands (one per story), typing the phrase **`mint`** each time.
4. Only after that ceremony + a digest chore PR did Wave1 dispatch continue.
5. Mid merge-path, Greptile residuals required `file_scope` expansion → agent again stopped for **`renewed-approval`** TTY ceremonies (again leave-harness).
6. Terminology (“mint”) does not match the human action (scope approval / change-ticket countersignature) and increases cognitive load.

### Why the agent did this (mechanism)

Current deposited guidance teaches agents that declared `file_scope` requires a **human-presence TTY digest on the merge base before implement**, and that expansion requires **`renewed-approval` on operator return**:

- `.deft/core/docs/scope-provenance.md` — mint on real TTY; commit digests before implement; expansion without renewal fails closed
- Consumer `AGENTS.md` managed section — same remint rule for declared `file_scope` expansion (#4589)
- Agents cannot mint (AUTHZ agent/CI markers refuse) — so the only compliance path is interrupting the human out-of-band

That is a coherent anti-forgery design, and it is the wrong session shape once review and merge are agentic. The recut below drops the scope ceremony. Proceed is the only human event. The fence is the brief already on the merge base. Class checks are #4980.

## Expected Results

1. After in-harness proceed, the cohort runs with zero leave-harness prompts. No scope ceremony is scheduled. This issue has no pre-Wave-1 root-count refusal.
2. The fence is the active brief's `file_scope` on the merge base. `verify:scope-provenance` reads that base copy. A pull request that adds production paths and edits its own active brief to include them fails `task check`. No digest is written.
3. Paths under a configured test root pass and spend nothing. The fence and the budget apply to production roots only.
4. One production call site outside the frozen list, within the cap, lands. Paths past the cap split to a follow-up story, with no prompt. The cap is a count of concrete production files on the merge base, floor 2, cap 5. Unrelated and low-confidence are not selectors. There is no digest and no scope phrase.
5. Class checks stay on #4980. This issue does not define them.

## Actual Results

1. Proceed consent did **not** authorize uninterrupted swarm execution.
2. Operator was interrupted **multiple times**, after delay, to leave the harness and run `scope:record-approved-scope` (first adoption ×4, renewed-approval ×2, plus a later m1-17 ask).
3. Each interruption required a real TTY, `--confirm`, and typed phrase **`mint`**.
4. Work continued only after digest chore PRs (#332, #337) landed digests on `main`.
5. Agent behavior matched deposited provenance docs/skills — so this is a **product/session-contract bug** (intent vs guidance), not a one-off agent hallucination.

## Suggested fix (recut 2026-09-23)

Operator note 5801277420 amends comment 5798533764. Review and merge on consumer repos are agentic. A control that needs a human to read a list or a diff is not a control. Class checks are split to #4980. This issue keeps the fence, the proceed contract, and the budget.

1. No scope record. Nothing writes `.deft/approved-scope/` for this path. `isHumanApprovalStamp` is not involved. The phrase `mint` stays on `authz:grant` only.
2. The fence is the active brief's `file_scope` as it stands on the merge base. `verify:scope-provenance` reads that base copy, not the head brief. The planner's declaration is on the base before the worker branches. The worker is a later process and cannot widen that base list.
3. Test roots are free. New tests, fixtures, helpers, and integration tests under a configured test root spend no budget. The fence and the budget apply to production roots only.
4. Production paths inside the cap land. Paths past the cap split to a follow-up story. The cap is a count of concrete production files on the merge base, floor 2, cap 5. No prompt. Unrelated and low-confidence are not selectors. `scopeExpansion` does not send the session to `scope:record-approved-scope --kind renewed-approval`.
5. `scope-provenance.md`, `deft-directive-swarm`, and the AGENTS managed text say: after proceed, do not stop for scope. There is no scope ceremony.

Not in this fix: a batch mint, a harness attestation, a digest, a rename of `mint` while the ceremony remains, a pre-Wave-1 root-count refusal, an unrelated or low-confidence split, reopening the #4589 remint, or a role check. The #4589 renewal path is retired. Placement failures and protected globs are #4980.

## Related

- #4980 — fail-closed class checks, split from this issue
- #4383 — setup scopes born without `file_scope`; mint lands mid-build (planning/setup path)
- #4589 / #4599 — `file_scope` expansion renewal remint after operator left; this recut retires that path
- #3718 — `swarm:launch` / readiness / `file_scope` vs provenance collision
- #3638 — TTY-free `--dry-run/--explain` of what mint would bind (partial relief only)
- #3145 — the class of change the class checks hold
- #3110 / #3384 — the grant phrase and the human stamp, which stay off this path
- Consumer dogfood: NoteTechnic cohort `m1-13-17` (2026-09-22/23), pin 0.119.6

## Acceptance (for the fix)

- [ ] Operator proceed on an N-story cohort produces zero leave-harness prompts. No scope ceremony is scheduled. This issue has no pre-Wave-1 root-count refusal.
- [ ] A pull request that adds production paths and edits its own active xBRIEF to include them fails `task check` with no digest anywhere.
- [ ] A worker adds `tests/…/test_writer.py` and a fixture under a configured test root: passes, nothing spent.
- [ ] One production call site outside the frozen list, within the cap, lands. Paths past the cap split to a follow-up story, with no prompt. The cap is a count of concrete production files on the merge base, floor 2, cap 5. Unrelated and low-confidence are not selectors.
- [ ] `scope-provenance.md`, `deft-directive-swarm`, and the AGENTS managed text say: after proceed, do not stop for scope; there is no scope ceremony to schedule.
- [ ] Dogfood: the NoteTechnic M1-13..17 cohort replays from proceed to PR-ready with zero prompts and no chore digest PRs.
